column2: The new drill is a hard one: pikes and halberds in close order, handgunners firing by ranks, a charge of horse to test the line. You ride the front yourself to show the men how it is done. A horse shies, a pike swings wide, and the next thing you know you are on your back in the mud with the surgeon kneeling over you.
The wound will heal. The drill goes on.
I will carry this mark for the rest of my days.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

A word from the drill yard: I was hurt while putting the men through a new formation. It is a clean wound and the surgeon says I will mend. The drill goes on without me until I can sit a horse again.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

My liege,

A word from the drill yard: I was hurt while putting the men through a new formation, and the surgeon could not save all of me. I am still your marshal and I will still serve, though I will never again lead a charge the way I did.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Such is the price of a strong army.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] keeps the finest soldiers in the province, and everyone knows why. [From.GetSheHeCap] has drill books of [From.GetHerHis] own, copied from veterans of a dozen campaigns: how to hold a square against cavalry, how to march a column through a forest without losing half of it. If [From.GetSheHe] could be talked into sharing them...
I will ask [From.GetHerHim] myself.
The lord will be asked to share the drill books.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], marshal of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has called on you with wine and compliments. What [From.GetSheHe] really wants are your drill books, which have cost you years of campaigning to put together.
Take them, and use them well.
Some secrets stay in the family.
The marshal will learn the lord's secrets.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent over [From.GetHerHis] drill books, bound in old leather and full of notes in the margins. Half of it you knew already. The other half will change the way the army fights.
My liege must hear of this generosity.
Your liege will gain the secrets.

My liege,

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has shared [FromFrom.GetHerHis] drill books with me, and I have already begun teaching their lessons to the men. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] deserves your thanks.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
A loyal subject indeed.

The drills of the past months have paid off. Word has spread that the liege's marshal feeds the men well and pays on time, and fresh levies keep turning up at the muster: farmers' sons, discharged mercenaries and a few men nobody asks too many questions about.
More spears for the realm.
The province will refill its levies faster.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] reports that the drill has drawn fresh men to the muster in [From.Location.GetName]. The levies there will be quick to fill again.
Good work, Marshal.

You have come to drill the levies of [From.Location.GetName], but one of the lords there keeps finding reasons why [From.GetHerHis] men cannot come: the harvest, a fever, a broken bridge. Nobody believes a word of it. [From.GetSheHeCap] simply does not want [From.GetHerHis] men learning to march to the liege's drum.
Send [From.GetHerHim] a sharp letter.
The lord will answer.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] writes, in the name of your liege, that your levies are to report for drill without further delay. The tone is not friendly.
My men stay on my land.
Very well. Let them march.
The marshal will write to the liege.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] refuses to send [From.GetHerHis] levies to the drill. I have done what I can, but [From.GetSheHe] answers my letters with excuses and insults. The men of [FromFrom.Location.GetName] will be slow to answer your call to arms until this is settled.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
[From.GetSheHeCap] will regret this.

Word went round the longhouses that the liege wants fighting men, and they came: young warriors who have never taken a head, old ones who have run out of plunder, outlaws who want their names back. They are eager, they are hungry and they are already asking where the raiding is.
Follow me to our chief!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has brought a war band to your hall, raised from every corner of the land. They will follow you wherever there is loot, but they will not sit idle for long.
Then let us find them something to burn.

The raiders [From.GetTitledFirstName] raised for you have sat by your fires for months, eating your food and waiting for the raid you promised. Now they have had enough. Before they go home they want what they are owed, and they make it clear that they will take it one way or another.
Pay them and be rid of them.
